title: Type IIB Axion--Dilaton Wormholes and the BPS Limit Hessian
abstract: I revisit Type-IIB axion--dilaton Euclidean saddles in a specified axion charge sector. In that sector, the solution with $E=0$ is the BPS instanton, while $E>0$ gives non-BPS wormholes with a smooth throat. The two cases solve the same radial equations but define different fluctuation problems. For the $E=0$ instanton, the Hamiltonian constraint, gauge quotient, charge-sector boundary condition, and removal of collective zero modes reduce the quadratic action to a physical Hessian. This Hessian factorizes, $ {\cal H}_ν={\mathcal Q}_ν^\dagger{\mathcal Q}_ν$. I interpret this as an endpoint theorem, beyond a stability theorem for the full $E>0$ wormhole. This puts Type IIB wormhole spectra on firmer grounds. I also separate the connected two-ended wormhole throat from its long-distance two-end multipole operator term. Once the coefficient matrix $C^{ij}$ is derived, the different-component and same-component placements of the two end insertions are terms in the same quadratic expression. Removing either term requires a genuine projection or cancellation.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes Type-IIB axion-dilaton wormholes, distinguishing between stable BPS instantons and unstable non-BPS wormhole deformations. The core mathematical achievement is proving that the fluctuation spectrum around the BPS endpoint factorizes into a simple quadratic form of an operator $Q^\dagger Q$. This provides strong structural constraints on quantum gravity solutions.
main_problem: The paper revisits Type-IIB axion--dilaton Euclidean saddles, comparing the BPS instanton ($E=0$) to non-BPS wormholes ($E>0$). It aims to provide a rigorous understanding of the spectrum and stability of these gravitational solutions.

method: The methodology involves variational analysis of the Euclidean action, deriving radial equations, and applying constraint solving (Hamiltonian/gauge fixing) to reduce the quadratic fluctuation action to a physical Hessian operator.
model_or_system: The system is Type IIB string theory compactified on geometries supporting axion-dilaton fields. The analysis covers both asymptotically flat 4D and AdS$_5$ backgrounds, treating wormholes as deformations of BPS instantons.

important_parameters: Energy parameter $E$ (determining BPS vs. non-BPS); neck radius $a_c$; and background curvature scales (e.g., AdS length scale).
main_assumptions: The Hessian factorization theorem is strictly proven only for the physical domain corresponding to the $E=0$ BPS instanton, not necessarily for the full $E>0$ wormhole stability.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the general Euclidean action and radial equations. It then focuses on deriving the physical Hessian for the BPS endpoint ($E=0$) via constraint imposition, demonstrating its factorization. Finally, it compares this result to non-BPS wormholes and discusses dimensional reductions (4D vs AdS$_5$).
why_interesting: While highly specialized in quantum gravity, the rigorous mathematical techniques used—such as deriving physical operators by eliminating constrained degrees of freedom (Schur complement) and proving spectral properties via operator factorization—are analogous to methods used in effective field theories or open quantum systems.
